problem.text: The base-nine representation of the number $N$ is $27{,}006{,}000{,}052_{\text{nine}}$. What is the remainder when $N$ is divided by $5$?

steps.title: Where to start: write $N$ as a sum of powers of $9$
steps.body: We only want a remainder, so we never need the huge base-ten value of $N$. A base-nine number is a sum of its digits times powers of $9$, and remainders can be worked out term by term. So first write out that sum, keeping only the nonzero digits.

your_turn.prompt: The number has $11$ digits. Which power of $9$ goes with the leading digit $2$, and which nonzero digits are left?
your_turn.answer: The leading $2$ goes with $9^{10}$. The other nonzero digits are $7$ (with $9^9$), $6$ (with $9^6$), $5$ (with $9^1$) and $2$ (with $9^0$).

steps.title: Replace $9$ by something small
steps.body: So $$N = 2\cdot 9^{10} + 7\cdot 9^9 + 6\cdot 9^6 + 5\cdot 9 + 2.$$ Since $9 = 10 - 1$, the number $9$ leaves the same remainder as $-1$ when divided by $5$. So in every term we may put $-1$ in place of $9$ without changing the remainder.

your_turn.prompt: What is $(-1)^k$ when $k$ is even, and when $k$ is odd?
your_turn.answer: $1$ when $k$ is even and $-1$ when $k$ is odd.

steps.title: Add up the signed digits
steps.body: After the swap, each term becomes its digit times $+1$ or $-1$, depending on whether the exponent is even or odd. Careful: $9$ is not $1$ modulo $5$, so you cannot just add the digits as you would when dividing by $8$.

your_turn.prompt: Which of the digits $2, 7, 6, 5, 2$ get a minus sign?
your_turn.answer: The $7$ (exponent $9$) and the $5$ (exponent $1$), because those exponents are odd. The two $2$s and the $6$ keep a plus sign.

steps.title: Put it together
steps.body: So $N$ leaves the same remainder as $2 - 7 + 6 - 5 + 2 = -2$ when divided by $5$. A remainder must be between $0$ and $4$, so add $5$: $-2 + 5 = 3$. The answer is **(D)**.

wrong_choices.C: This comes from adding the digits, $2+7+6+5+2 = 22$, which leaves $2$. That treats $9$ as $1$ modulo $5$, but $9$ leaves remainder $4$, which acts like $-1$, so the signs must alternate. Dropping the minus sign of $-2$ also lands here.
